item.title: A Photo Book of Murderers
item.content:encoded:
Idea Post:

Seeking Greenlights: Primarily Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror a lot, Drama/Emotional a good deal, History a little.

Page Layout (Optional): Basic special containment procedures and description followed by how it was obtained, then testing logs, and finally incident reports (maybe).

Elevator Pitch: Photobook slash journal used by a former researcher working at an asylum (the early ’50s to ’70s) studying primarily murderous and violent patients. People who place a photo in the book begin to have their memories and their personalities overwritten with psychotic patients.

Central Narrative: I want to highlight the malpractices and the sickening practices of asylums that studied the brains of ‘psychotic’ individuals. Reports of weird experiments have always been rumored and very few reports survive from these places because some of these acts were perpetrated by leading scientists who used this research to better our understanding of psychology. There are even reports of human sacrifices and brutal use of pagan rituals and some real dark sh. Whether or not these are real stories says what if they were really basically.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is unique in my opinion are the stories the imprinted patients can tell to people, the horrors they experienced, and how it happened.

Additional Notes: I know there are no factual claims to the horrors of such asylums in real life but I just want to tell the story, please don’t come to tell me why it isn't factual. It's SCP it ain’t meant to be factual it's meant to be fun!

item.title: A House Dividing - idea I'd love critiques/greenlights for
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): SCP research article with addendums about the experiments conducted.

Elevator Pitch: An old, abandoned house in New Hampshire with a room upstairs. If you're in the room and can't reach the door it will snap shut and anyone inside disappears. At the exact same moment, four exact copies of that person or those people, linked through physical experience, are generated in four random places on the planet, with one of them in mortal peril and the rest left to experience the death as an introduction to their new, linked experience.

Central Narrative: the house generates people who share physical experiences, and immediately causes one of them to be placed into a situation where they will die. Some of the experiments done on the room after it's discovery had mixed results, however research would have been paused after a character that I think would be useful for other things would be the sole survivor, the three other copies dying within days of their creation. Outside of the death at the beginning, which shocks many who experience it, the three share physical experiences and can communicate in limited fashion with each other. The Foundation experiments with the SCP, first confirming it's safety as well as confirming the sanity and normality of the copies before making a small team of operators, three copies of the same agent, using the SCP after it's experimentation shows it's safe status. That status is revoked when the second person sent through, a higher level operator specializing in Keter Class wet work, becomes the 'sole survivor.' Rather than experiencing a coming together of support and love of his other copies after grieving together, creating a unit far more capable than most, the Sole Survivor experiences their death three times and has a mental breakdown, joining the Chaos.

I have more details/ideas written out as a draft of sorts if you want a link.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: a house in the middle of nowhere that creates linked copies of people random places around the planet and connects their physical experiences.

item.title: Re: It just doesn't feel, "SCP" enough.
item.content:encoded:
Oh No! When editing I took out the lines where I explained what I meant by "encourages you to act on your intrusive thoughts!" So, intrusive thoughts are thoughts that you have impulsively. More often than not these thoughts are violent. People who have been affected by this "magic earworm" have committed acts from strange but harmless behavior all the way up to homicide and self-mutilation. This was actually inspired by something that happened to me the other day. I was cooking and chopping onions and I was singing a song in my head, when an intrusive thought popped up and said "chop your finger off." I started singing "chop your finger off" to the tune of the song that was stuck in my head. I feel so dumb for leaving out the explanation. I was erasing fluff lines to stay under the word count but I must have erased the wrong ones.

Also, I'm glad you asked about if it can appear randomly. Yes it absolutely can. That is how the phenomenon starts in Patient 0, seemingly at random. The Foundation has contained at least a dozen outbreaks in the past, all in different areas around the world. Usually, these outbreaks are 5-10 years apart from each other and leads credence to the "phenomenon theory." However, the past three outbreaks have all been within the past three years. The staff that believes in the "entity theory "believes the entity is going through a sort of molting period, they believe that this entity feeds on sanity and is about to evolve. So it requires more sustenance and is moving at a much faster rate. In the original findings, people who had the "Jukebug" could not transmit it through recordings, and it was safe to record any singing the afflicted did. However within the past three years, the "Jukebug" phenomenon or entity has evolved to be able to spread through audio and visual recording, so the Foundation has revoked clearance for recording.

I know it seems like a lot I left out in the pitch, however I wanted the basics explained first, which I apparently failed to do. Thank you for your input and for taking the time to read this.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: Conehead
item.content:encoded:
This is one of those bizarre ideas I believe definitely belongs on this site at some point. I love the creativity and thought that you put into this. I know this is just an idea critique forum, but if you're seeking green light, my suggestion to you would be to work on your clinical tone and your grammar. For example, "Weirdly enough, it has no body parts except for limbs and the torso, and head. The bottom of its feet where you would usually find paws, is just more fur." This could be written in a way that makes it stronger, "The entity posses all four limbs, but lacks extremities such as paws. Instead the legs end in stubs, balanced on balled up, matted fur. The entity also lacks any visible orifices, or genitalia. This implies the anomaly lacks any digestive track or endocrine system typical of a domesticated canine."

Because the idea is so bizarre and frankly a little funny/cute, I think the best way to get this SCP ready for green light is to rework your idea presentation. Show us you can make this idea draft work in that clinical tone as best as possible to amplify the strengths of your idea.

I truly hope to be scrolling through the articles and stumble across this one day. Thank you for sharing!

item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5127 (Also known as The Cannibal) will eat anything within sight. However, it is worried to eat things around other humans. It appears to be a tall white figure with a very skinny stomach. It’s face features eye sockets that are completely black and a large mouth with shark-like teeth. When it is around humans (as previously mentioned) it gets worried and it’s eye sockets begin to look angry. It gets rid of humans by breathing out air that causes them to open the door and attempt to let the scp free. The human who breathed in the air then kills them self (see incident 5127-A). The creature can eat a full metal door within 15 seconds. As such, we have made a door made out of diamond. The creature eats the diamond door within a 15 day period. The door must be replaced within 10 days as it is then possible for the creature to escape. The creature seems to like wood. As such, we give it 500 planks of wood a day. A human who attempts to harm the creature is eaten by it.

Deleted at -19 and three votes.

SCP-5295 is a faded white porcelain flush toilet estimated to date from the mid-1980s. A mostly faded stamp on the side of the cistern indicates the manufacturer to be █████. In appearance and physical composition it is unremarkable.

Deleted at -14 and three votes.

I mean, fine, it's kind of weird for someone to have six whole chickens in their refrigerator, but I don't see the significance of that as it relates to the narrative. item.title: Re: SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Well, to start I really like the name, Arkansas Creek Walker. I think that's really unique and totally sounds like a cryptid people would believe in, in the Arkansas region. I personally would be fascinated to read more about this. That being said- I think this is really similar to SCP-906, right on down to the tenacity of chasing prey. I think what would make your SCP stand out from 906 would be if the swarm had one single, sentient consciousness.

The difference between a hive mind and single, sentient consciousness would be something like the following:

Hive mind: "Look out, it's a swarm of bugs shaped like a man."
Single mind: " Look out, it's a man, made out of bugs."

However, once you move into the single-mind side of things you start to risk X-Man syndrome. So keep an eye out for that.
As for what should be the cause of this, I grew up in Alaska. In my native culture we had this legend of 3 brothers who were kidnapped by a cannibal giant in the woods. The first two brothers were eaten but the third brother killed the giant and burned his body. The ashes flew into the sky and became the mosquitos. Maybe, that's something you could work with.

Anyhow, I really do like this idea and I'm very interested to see where you take it!

item.title: SCP - The Infinite Quarter
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-#### “The Infinite Quarter” is a 2019 San Antonio Mission Texas Quarter with the head side scratched out with a unknown instrument. The quarter seems like an average coin but when left unobserved the coin will start to rapidly multiply until observed or all open space is occupied. All other instances of the scp do not share the same anomalous duplication ability as the main coin and will only share the ability of ceasing duplication when the coins are observed though if one were to observe a duplicated instance of the coin and not the original coin it will not stop the original from duplicating.

Central Narrative: The coin would of first been discovered when foundation agents caught wind of a man who seemed to of out of the blue came into a fortune oddly enough in quarters. Upon investigating and obvious administration of amnestic, they discovered a shoe box completely full of quarters. It wasn’t until the agent investigating the box looked away and then back to discover that the box had begun to overflow with quarters before stopping. After finding the anomalous coin they brought it to the foundation and contain it in a specially made plastic case big enough to fit a single quarter.

** Hook/Attention-Grabber:** All duplicated instances of the coin will be in perfect condition and not sharing any of the scratch marks on the head side of the coin like the original does. I had also thought to make it so that the actual original coin is always the easiest to spot as to make it more easier to be observed to warrant its duplication stopping when viewed.

** Additional notes:** possible idea is the scp foundation will sometimes use this scp for possible funding for resources and the like.

item.title: SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: Horror.

Elevator Pitch: A strange, humanoid mass of vampiric insects has been tormenting parts of America.

Central Narrative: Wild animal population has been decreasing rapidly as of late in the Southwest part of America, as well as hunters. Something strange is happening, and farmers in the area have seen it in front row seats.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The bugs are mosquitoes. Not any normal mosquitoes, though. They are omnivorous, and will dig through any biological material to get some meat. This means it will eat through wood, dirt, and any other greens, but not stone-like substances.

Additional Notes: I just want to know if there should be anything that could possibly be leading the entity other than just being a paranormal happenstance.

As for writing, just make sure you go through the proper greenlighting process on the idea forums first. Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you! For my recommendation, you should check out SCP-4054 its an anomalous NES game, what could go wrong?

+ Resources
- Hide Resources

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerened, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.

Best of luck!

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
+ Open for critique
- Behold!

Preface: I am not a trans person, my critique is not going to be about the potential sensitivity of the article as I am not a good source to judge how it will affect trans people.

My opinion on this right now is that it's somewhat hollow as well as overlong. There is some horror imagery here, specifically:

When SCP-XXXX-2’s head has become engulfed, direct respiration, as well as the direct consumption of food and drink, becomes impossible. SCP-XXXX will provide SCP-XXXX-2 with an intravenous supply of oxygen, nutrition, and hydration, however the amounts supplied are suboptimal for survival.

and

This sheath grows from the attachment site at the back of the neck, over the head, and eventually covers the entire body. SCP-XXXX’s underdeveloped eye and mouth structures move to the front of SCP-XXXX-2’s head and become enlarged. Upon completion of this process, SCP-XXXX is considered to have entered its adult phase.

I do like the ending, but yet it feels hollow at the same time. I believe this is because the entirety of this article is a cold description of the anomaly and what it does. Not that these types of descriptions don't work, more that it's the issue at hand should be explored on a more personal level. If I'm reading this correctly, SCP-XXXX is the embodiment of transphobia, dysphoria, and self-hate. A cold, clinical description doesn't really convey that in a meaningful way.

My advice is to cut everything after the bulleted list and have the article pivot to either interview logs with an SCP-XXXX-2 instance. These would serve to show how SCP-XXXX functions on -2 while also providing the audience with a connection to this character. The ending you also have would have a bit more punch to it if we see these Foundation doctors supporting this character and their gender identity

cybersqyd recommended reaching out to more reviewers and I have to agree with ver on that.

Good luck!

item.title: Re: Psychological Theories in 1800s
item.content:encoded:
Sent you a PM.

In short, psychotherapy for mental illness (and even modern conceptions of mental illness as something with (partially) psychological and relationship-based causes rather than just a moral, spiritual, or physical cause) did not exist until the 1880's. Some of the people who Freud worked under in the 1880's were experimenting with hypnosis for "hysteria", but Freud was the first person to have a systematic theory and practice of therapy.

Before that in the 1800's, even the idea that mental illness had a physical/neurological cause, or the idea that people with mental illness might get better if you talk to them/don't treat them like complete shit/don't chain them up, were new ideas.

In terms of theories, most people were still basing theories on philosophy, most were interested in "normal" functioning people rather than mental illness, and the field of medicine itself was way less developed than it is now. Early psychologists were also more interested in studying "normal" perception and consciousness than abnormal psych (but, again, didn't exist as a separate field of study until the 1870s).

"Animal Magnetism" was a theory in the 1700's/early 1800's that led into hypnosis, but that was a theory of general human health/functioning and wasn't applied to mental illness until the 1880's. You could look at the Humors and Phrenology for ideas before that, but again, these were physical theories (with physical treatments in the case of humors) not "therapy."

Here are some links:
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigmund_Freud
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_Meynert
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Martin_Charcot
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Pinel

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_psychiatry (read the early modern part)

Edit: Also, the British aristocracy really cratered because of WW1, so you're free to set your SCP in the 1890-1910 range. If you do that, here are a few other things to look at:
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightner_Witmer
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Kraepelin

item.title: Re: Help. I posted my SCP but it says access denied.
item.content:encoded:
Alright, so what you have to do is go to the series page in question, and scroll to the bottom of the page. There, you should be able to see a series of red buttons; the furthermost one on the left being the word "edit". Click that, and scroll through the edit box to the slot № that you applied your article to ( * [[[SCP-5129]]] - [ACCESS DENIED] ).

Delete the text that says "[ACCESS DENIED]" and add whatever title you want. Do not change anything else on the page. Once finished, you can click save, and that's it. For the .aic elements like Secretary_Helen or CROM, it may take around 5 minutes to update, but Wikidot will do so instantly.
